name: MD-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+30 partisan lean makes the district deeply Democratic
Raskin holds an $8.1M-to-$3K cash-on-hand advantage over Riley
Polymarket prices a Democratic win at 97%
No general-election polling; fundamentals and money dominate
model.rationale: The district's thirty-point Democratic lean, Raskin's overwhelming financial edge, and market pricing near ninety-seven percent for Democrats all point to a safe seat, with no polls or ratings suggesting any competitive threat.
model.watch: A major external event or unexpected national wave could narrow the margin, though the outcome itself is very unlikely to come into question.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Maryland's 8th District leans Democratic by thirty points, and Jamie Raskin enters the general election as a heavily favored incumbent. He has raised more than nine million dollars and holds over eight million on hand, while Republican Cheryl Riley has raised about twenty-two thousand with roughly three thousand remaining. A Green Party candidate is also on the ballot but lacks visible resources. Prediction markets price the Democratic side near ninety-seven percent.

No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the fundraising gap, and market pricing. The combination points to a comfortable Democratic win, with the main question being the size of the margin rather than the outcome. Barring an unexpected external event, this seat is not considered competitive this cycle.
